articles.summary: Bet365 te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Barcelona y al Feyenoord en el Spotify Camp Nou correspondiente al debut de ambos en la fase liga de la Champions League
articles.body: El Barcelona recibe al Feyenoord este miércoles en el Spotify Camp Nou, en el partido correspondiente a la primera jornada de la fase liga de la Champions League 26/27, en la que el conjunto azulgrana quiere trasladar a Europa el arrollador estado de forma mostrado en LaLiga. El equipo de Hansi Flick llega tras golear 0-5 al Valencia en Mestalla, con doblete de Lamine Yamal y goles de Fermín López, Raphinha y Pedri, resultado que le mantiene con pleno de victorias y 17 goles a favor en sus cuatro primeras jornadas ligueras. Favorito para el partido entre Barcelona y Feyenoord Por su parte, el Feyenoord llega a Barcelona con la confianza reforzada tras una sólida victoria por 3-1 en su visita al NEC Nijmegen en la Eredivisie, resultado que le permite presentarse en el Camp Nou con buenas sensaciones pese a la enorme dificultad del reto. El conjunto neerlandés, campeón de Europa en 1970, arrastra sin embargo una estadística preocupante de cara a este desplazamiento. No gana fuera de casa en competición europea desde hace once partidos, una racha que el Camp Nou no se presenta precisamente como el mejor escenario para cortar. Con todos estos datos, las casas de apuestas dan como claro favorito al Barcelona. Bet365 paga la victoria azulgrana a cuota 1.09, por 10 del empate y 21 de la victoria del cuadro neerlandés. El Feyenoord acumula 41 compromisos europeos consecutivos marcando gol, una racha que da idea de su potencial ofensivo pese a jugar como visitante, mientras que el Barcelona no ha dejado su portería a cero en ninguno de sus últimos partidos de Champions, con 43 encuentros seguidos sin terminar 0-0 en el torneo. Con estos datos, según las apuestas deportivas, la probabilidad de que ambos equipos anoten es alta. Bet365 paga a 1.80 el "sí" y a 1.95 el "no". Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta hacia un partido con mucha producción ofensiva. El Barcelona ha marcado 17 tantos en sus cuatro primeros partidos de liga, una media que invita a pensar en un marcador amplio, mientras que el Feyenoord también ha demostrado capacidad goleadora tanto en su liga como en Europa. Con estos datos, Bet365 sitúa la cuota del +2.5 totales a 1.17, por 5 del caso contrario. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners se presenta como una alternativa interesante para los apostantes. El Barcelona, con su juego de posesión y dominio territorial marcado por Flick, suele generar un volumen muy alto de saques de esquina en el Camp Nou, algo que quedó patente en sus últimas salidas ligueras. El Feyenoord, por su parte, se verá obligado a replegarse buena parte del partido ante la superioridad azulgrana, lo que invita a pensar en una notable diferencia de córners a favor del conjunto local en este debut europeo. articles.title: Real Madrid beat Inter Milan as Mbappe goal sets Mourinho’s men on way
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe opens the scoring but Real Madrid fail to convince in 2-1 Champions League win against Inter Milan.
articles.body:
Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid secured a narrow 2-1 victory over his former side, Inter Milan, in a high-octane Champions League opener on Tuesday.

The record 15-time European champions took a two-goal lead through Kylian Mbappe and Fede Valverde thanks to two Inter errors in the first half.

Carlos Augusto smashed home for Cristian Chivu’s team in the second half but they could not find an equaliser at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Madrid coach Mourinho led the Italian side to Champions League glory in 2010 at the same stadium, the last time either they or he managed to lift the trophy, a few days before joining Los Blancos for his first stint at the helm.

After two seasons without a major trophy and enduring early European exits, Madrid President Florentino Perez brought back the Portuguese veteran to try and stop the rot, and Mourinho got the team off to both a triumphant and entertaining start to the league phase.

Mourinho’s side bounced back from a first defeat of the season at Real Betis in La Liga on Friday, although goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois made several smart saves and Inter were wasteful.

The Italians started energetically in attack but were destabilised by two grievous errors at the back. Madrid stopper Courtois denied Marcus Thuram and then Lautaro Martinez as the visitors probed.

However, in the 14th minute Curtis Jones’s poor pass put Yann Bisseck under pressure and Brahim Diaz poked the ball through to Mbappe, who swiftly fired home.

Madrid’s second was gobbled up by Valverde when Inter goalkeeper Josep Martinez dallied on the ball despite the Uruguay international charging straight for him.

When the Spanish stopper realised it was too late and as he tried to turn, Valverde pried the ball away from him and into the net.

Mourinho’s side should have added another before half-time but Martinez made amends for his mistake with a sensational save to thwart Jude Bellingham.

Mbappe blazed past Inter’s defence and Martinez saved his low shot before somehow blocking Bellingham’s effort from point-blank range.

Bellingham missed another golden chance before the hour mark after Diaz cleverly worked his way into the area and crossed for him.

The England international might have headed home straight away but chose to control the ball and gave goalkeeper Martinez time to fly across his line and save the eventual shot.

Courtois added to his collection of impressive saves by pushing away Alessandro Bastoni’s low drive as Inter tried to find a foothold.

Madrid carved Inter open but could not put the game to bed, with Martinez saving from Mbappe and Diaz then sliding narrowly wide.

Carlos Augusto blasted past Courtois from Lautaro Martinez’s cross in the 77th minute to give Madrid a nervy ending to the game.

Madrid fans were upset when Alvaro Carreras was made to wait for a minute on the sidelines before he could come on as a substitute, because Vinicius Jr took too long to come off when he was replaced.

Courtois beat away a deflected Henrikh Mkhitaryan effort to ensure his team took all three points.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal scripts Ballon d’Or history, becomes first player to be nominated three times before turning 20
articles.summary: Football News: Lamine Yamal has made history as the first player to receive three Ballon d'Or nominations before turning 20, showcasing his incredible talent with Barcelona and the Spanish national team. His achievements include a significant role in Spain's 2026 World Cup victory and multiple domestic titles with Barcelona, as he continues to break records at an extraordinary young age.
articles.body: Lamine Yamal has made Ballon d'Or history after becoming the first player ever to receive three nominations for the prestigious award before turning 20.The Barcelona forward was included in the 30-player shortlist for the 2026 Ballon d'Or, announced on September 8, giving him a nomination for the third consecutive year after also making the shortlist in 2024 and 2025.Yamal, who was born on July 13, 2007, in Mataró, Spain, is still only 19, but has already established himself as one of the most prominent players in world football for both FC Barcelona and Spain.The achievement is different from simply being nominated multiple times. Legendary figures including Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi have been nominated for the Ballon d'Or numerous times, while Yamal's distinction is the age at which he has accumulated his three nominations.He was also the youngest player ever nominated for the Ballon d'Or, breaking into the shortlist at just 17 years old in 2024.Yamal has now been nominated three years in a rowYamal's first Ballon d'Or nomination came in 2024, when he finished eighth in the voting after playing a key role in Spain's victory at the 2024 European Championship.A year later, he went even closer to winning the award.Yamal finished second in the 2025 Ballon d'Or, behind Paris Saint-Germain winger Ousmane Dembele, who had enjoyed a treble-winning campaign.His third consecutive nomination follows another outstanding season for both club and country.For Barcelona, Yamal scored 24 goals and provided 15 assists in 45 games across all competitions, helping Hansi Flick's side successfully defend their La Liga and Supercopa de España titles.He then played a significant role in Spain's victorious 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign in the United States, Canada and Mexico.Yamal featured in all seven matches of Spain's run to the World Cup title and scored, and assisted once apiece during the tournament. Spain defeated 10-man defending champions Argentina in the final in New Jersey in July to win their second World Cup.That success has added further weight to Yamal's case for the 2026 Ballon d'Or, after he had already collected major honours at both club and international level.His club honours include three La Liga titles in 2023, 2025 and 2026, as well as the 2025 domestic treble.Individually, he has won the Kopa Trophy in both 2024 and 2025, making him the only player in football history to win the award for the world's best young player in consecutive years, making him the only player in football history to win the award for the world's best young player in consecutive years.Yamal has already rewritten Spain's record booksYamal's record-breaking Ballon d'Or achievement is only the latest in a series of milestones he has reached at an extraordinarily young age.He has earned 33 caps for Spain's senior national team and scored seven goals, having become an established figure for La Roja before his 20th birthday.His international career began with another historic achievement.Yamal became Spain's youngest-ever player and youngest-ever goalscorer when he made his senior debut against Georgia on September 8, 2023, aged just 16 years and 57 days.He went on to win the Euro 2024, the 2025 UEFA Nations League and the 2026 World Cup with Spain.His World Cup campaign also saw him start all seven matches as Spain completed their historic run to the title, making him one of the youngest World Cup winners in football history.The 2026 Ballon d'Or nomination comes after an equally impressive start to the new club season.Yamal drew a blank as Barcelona began their campaign with a 5-0 victory at Elche and again in the 2-0 home win over Athletic Club, before scoring twice in a 3-2 home victory over Rayo Vallecano.He then scored another two goals as Barcelona defeated Valencia 5-0 away from home at the weekend, a result that moved Flick's side three points clear at the top of the fledgling La Liga standings.Barcelona's next challenge is against Feyenoord at home on September 9, 10:15 PM IST, as they begin their quest for a first UEFA Champions League title in more than a decade.Yamal's third Ballon d'Or nomination therefore arrives at a remarkable point in his career. He has already been the youngest nominee in the award's history, finished eighth and then second, won back-to-back Kopa Trophies, collected major domestic and international honours and helped Spain become world champions.Now, before even turning 20, he has become the first player ever to receive three Ballon d'Or nominations at that age.The 2026 ceremony will take place on Monday, October 26, 2026, at the London Palladium Theatre in London, marking the first time the Ballon d'Or ceremony will be held outside Paris.Alongside Yamal, the 30-player shortlist features leading names including defending winner Ousmane Dembélé, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappé and 39-year-old Lionel Messi, with the winner set to be crowned in London.For Yamal, however, the nomination itself has already secured another unique place in Ballon d'Or history.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mouriño carga contra el árbitro: "Se sintió presionado por el campo y pitó penalti"
articles.standfirst: El defensa uruguayo lamenta el penalti señalado en contra en el tramo final del partido ante el Borussia Dortmund: "Perdemos por un error arbitral"
articles.summary: El defensa uruguayo lamenta el penalti señalado en contra en el tramo final del partido ante el Borussia Dortmund: "Perdemos por un error arbitral"
articles.body: Santiago Mouriño se mostró muy enfadado con la actuación arbitral tras la derrota del Villarreal frente al Borussia Dortmund (3-2). El defensa uruguayo consideró errónea la pena máxima señalada en su contra en el minuto 83, una acción que permitió al conjunto alemán ampliar su ventaja (era el 3-1) desde los once metros y encarrilar el triunfo en el Signal Iduna Park. En declaraciones a Movistar+ al término del encuentro, Mouriño aseguró que el resultado estuvo condicionado por esa decisión. "Creo que hoy perdemos por error arbitral, porque por lo que se habla no fue penalti. Estamos jugando Champions League, hay mucho contacto. Por un doble agarre en el área, que él me agarra y yo lo agarro, pita penalti y nos hace perder un partido. Así es muy difícil competir", afirmó el zaguero del conjunto castellonense. El internacional uruguayo insistió en que la acción fue un forcejeo habitual dentro del área y fue más allá al valorar la actuación del colegiado italiano Simone Sozza. "Obviamente nos estábamos agarrando los dos. Yo creo que se sintió presionado por el campo y pitó penalti", señaló. La jugada protestada se produjo con 2-1 en el marcador, cuando Sozza señaló una infracción de Mouriño sobre Serhou Guirassy durante una acción a balón parado. El árbitro mostró además tarjeta amarilla al futbolista del Villarreal y concedió el lanzamiento desde los once metros, que el propio delantero guineano transformó en el 3-1. Más allá de la polémica, Mouriño lamentó que el Villarreal no aprovechara sus ocasiones cuando el marcador reflejaba el empate. "Hoy demostramos que podemos competir en todos los campos. Creo que fuimos mejor equipo en este campo, pero no pudimos llevarnos los tres puntos", comentó. Pese a la derrota, Mouriño destacó la actitud de su equipo en uno de los escenarios más exigentes del fútbol europeo. "Lo fuimos a buscar en todo momento. Creo que hicimos las cosas que vinimos a hacer acá y pudimos demostrarlo", concluyó el lateral uruguayo.

articles.title: Bartra: "El fútbol hoy ha sido justo con nosotros"
articles.standfirst: El central catalán, elegido MVP del partido frente al Lille con dos goles de cabeza
articles.summary: El central catalán, elegido MVP del partido frente al Lille con dos goles de cabeza
articles.body: Marc Bartra fue elegido el mejor jugador del partido frente al Lille, en Francia, en el que el Betis regresaba a la Champions League más de dos décadas después. Y no lo fue sólo por sus grandes acciones defensivas. También por lo que le aportó en ataque a los de Pellegrini, con dos goles de cabeza con los que el conjunto andaluz logró anular por dos veces la ventaja de los franceses. Así lo analizó en los micrófonos de Movistar Liga de Campeones. Gran regreso: "Noche soñada y me emociona porque al final creo que el fútbol también muchas veces es justo, y creo que ha sido muy justo con nosotros. Hemos remontado el partido de la manera que lo hemos hecho, encima meter dos, tres goles. Noche soñada. Se lo dedico a mis hijos, que es lo que más quiero en este mundo, y a toda esa gente que me ayuda, mis padres, mi hermano". Sus goles y el MVP: "Al final la Champions me trae muy buenos recuerdos desde pequeño y luego como jugador también del Barça, con el Dortmund. También con el Betis era un sueño poder llegar a jugar que se veía muy lejos y lo hemos cumplido. Ya llevo muchos años aquí y se lo dedico también a todos estos béticos. Al Betis lo amo, y poder jugar la Champions League y ganar de esta manera es una noche muy especial". Regañina de Pellegrini por subir a buscar el cuarto gol: "Al final veía que éramos uno más y poder ir a rematar el córner que al final quizá ya matábamos el partido metiendo el cuarto. Pero es verdad que el míster también me encanta porque al final gracias a él he mejorado muchísimo en muchos aspectos de mentalidad, en concentración, en lo defensivo. También se lo dedico, que sea el primero de muchos". Dónde colocará el trofeo de MVP: "Lo pondré en casa, en un buen sitio. Sí, de hecho tengo ahí también muchos trofeos de los que he ganado, réplicas entre medio de la Champions y demás. Los pondré seguramente allí y con la camiseta del Betis envolviéndolo".

articles.title: Raúl da un primer diagnóstico sobre el Madrid y Mourinho responde: "No sólo críticas..."
articles.standfirst: El técnico pareció algo molesto por el análisis del partido del exjugador madridista
articles.summary: El técnico pareció algo molesto por el análisis del partido del exjugador madridista
articles.body: La victoria del Real Madrid en el debut en Champions ante el Inter no dejó completamente satisfechos a los madridistas, que vieron cómo su equipo sufrió en el tramo final pese a haber gozado de muchas ocasiones claras de gol. Raúl González Blanco se estrenó como comentarista en Movistar con un análisis sobre la victoria del Real Madrid ante el Inter: "Lo mejor es que se ha conseguido los tres puntos, no ha sido fácil porque el Inter es un equipo con una estructura muy trabajada y el Madrid tenía bajas en el centro del campo". También también hizo un primer diagnóstico del sufrimiento blanco en los últimos minutos: "Llegaron los goles del Madrid por errores en la salida, luego ha tenido ocasiones muy claras y ese gol del Inter ha hecho que al final haya incertidumbre, pero resultado bueno para empezar la andadura". Inmediatamente la conexión se fue al Santiago Bernabéu, donde Jose Mourinho esperaba para dar su primera valoración en Movistar sobre el partido. Al técnico portugués le contaron el diagnóstico hecho por Raúl y pareció algo molesto, mirando a cámara al final de su discurso diciendo: "No sólo críticas, alguna cosa bien a nosotros". Mou, que durante algunas frases sufrió un lapsus y habló en italiano, analizó así el partido: "Prefiero decir que ha sido un partido loco, tantas veces hay críticas cuando el partido es aburrido, hoy que es loco... podía haber terminado 7-6 sin ningún problema. Teníamos un centro del campo debilitado, ellos han cambiado jugadores muy pronto y yo en el centro del campo no tenía mucho que hacer. Cuando he visto que los jugadores estaban en una situación difícil he cambiado, pero creo que los jugadores han hecho un gran trabajo. Aburrido no ha sido, hemos tenido para hacer el 3-0 en el último minuto del primer tiempo, pero estoy de acuerdo con Raúl que los goles llegan en un momento de errores de ellos, pero quiero dar crédito a los míos porque la presión se entrena, cómo presionar, dónde presionar, el trabajo y el gol de Valverde... es trabajo. No sólo críticas, alguna cosa bien a nosotros". Cuestionado por el poco control de sus jugadores, dijo: "Una cosa es que tú no tengas el control y ellos tampoco, el adversario tampoco lo tenía. Courtois ha parado mucho, pero ¿Cuántos goles hemos fallado en transición nosotros? Ha sido un gran partido". Y también desveló lo que le dijo a Vinicius en el momento de su cambio: "Ha trabajado mucho, muchísimo. Yo lo sé, todos lo sabemos, él lo sabe. No está todavía afilado, no está todavía Vinicius pero trabaja mucho y quien trabaja y da lo que tiene merece respeto".

articles.summary: El entrenador del Inter analizó la derrota ante el Madrid en rueda de prensa
articles.body: El Inter de Milán se estrenó en esta Champions con derrota. Los de Chivu lo intentaron en el Bernabéu, pero se toparon con una majestuosa versión de Courtois bajo palos. Chivu, entrenador de los italianos, analizó la derrota en rueda de prensa. Partido: "He visto a un equipo que ha tenido el balón y personalidad, conociendo lo que es el Real Madrid. Confío en que las cosas están funcionando, asumo también los errores. Hemos demostrado la actitud correcta, y arriesgando más. Hemos llegado muchas veces a su área. Asumo el valor y la personalidad de que no hemos venido a especular". Cómo aumentar la productividad: "Somos el equipo que hizo más de 100 goles el año pasado. Hoy hemos llegado, antes o después conseguiremos hacerlo mejor. Confío en la determinación de los jugadores. No estoy preocupado". Josep Martínez: "Me quedo con su reacción y personalidad. Lo que ha sido interesante es que se le ha venido encima. Nunca es fácil y ha hecho una gran prestación". Qué lección se lleva: "Que tenemos que seguir así. Saber levantarnos. Es lo que se me queda de esta noche y es lo que estoy intentando hacer". Partidos en los que no merece perder: "Tenemos todavía siete partidos para jugar. Volveremos a casa. A veces, es de forma no merecida, pero tenemos una plantilla competitiva y que quiere crecer. Nuestras ambiciones son altas e intentaremos mejorar en resultados".

articles.title: Lionel Messi set to buy second Spanish club, agrees 100% ownership of LaLiga 2 side CD Eldense: Report
articles.summary: Football News: Lionel Messi is set to expand his football ownership portfolio by acquiring 100% of CD Eldense, a LaLiga 2 club, marking a significant move in his post-playing career.
articles.body: Lionel Messi is reportedly preparing for another major step into football ownership, with the Argentina legend set to expand his business interests in Spain after making his first investment in the country's lower leagues earlier this year.The move would give the 39-year-old a direct stake in Spanish professional football while also taking him closer to the country where he spent the vast majority of his playing career and where he is expected to live after eventually ending his time as an active player with Inter Miami.Messi reportedly agrees deal to take full control of EldenseAccording to Marca, Messi has reached an agreement in principle with the current owners of CD Eldense to acquire the Alicante-based club.The reports state that Messi would acquire 100 per cent of Eldense's shares, meaning the investment would be made solely by the Argentine and would not involve partners, former players or other third parties.However, the agreement has not yet been completed.The deal is expected to be finalised in the coming days, provided the remaining legal and contractual formalities are completed. Those procedures include the necessary financial due diligence, while the proposed takeover will also require approval from the Spanish National Sports Council (CSD).The club is based in Elda, in Alicante province, and currently competes in LaLiga 2, Spain's second division. Eldense were recently promoted to the Segunda División, also known as LaLiga Hypermotion, for the 2026–27 season after winning Group 2 of the Primera Federación in May 2026, according to reports. The club currently has around 3,500 season-ticket holders.The proposed acquisition would represent another piece of Messi's emerging football business portfolio.Earlier in 2026, Messi acquired 100 per cent of the shares in UE Cornellà, a Catalan club competing in the Spanish third tier. That deal was announced in April, with Cornellà saying Messi's arrival would begin “a new chapter in the club’s history” aimed at driving sporting and institutional growth, strengthening its foundations and continuing investment in talent.The project at Cornellà has placed particular emphasis on youth academy development and women's football.The Eldense investment would take Messi's involvement to a considerably higher level of the Spanish football pyramid, with the club competing in professional football.The reports suggest the motivation behind the project is Messi's desire to invest his footballing legacy back into the game itself, with Eldense's location also potentially fitting into his longer-term plans.Elda is in Alicante province and is relatively close to Catalonia, where Messi is expected to live after his playing career comes to an end.Eldense takeover comes as club searches for new managerEldense was previously acquired by an international investment group with Colombian roots, led by businessman Juan Carlos Trujillo, who bought the club from Pascual Pérez in October 2015.There had already been speculation over a possible change of ownership in recent months, with Argentine businessman Ricardo Pini reportedly linked with a potential takeover worth around €12million.Messi's reported agreement has now changed the picture considerably, although the final transaction still needs to clear its remaining requirements before it can be considered complete.The club is also experiencing difficulties on the pitchEldense dismissed Claudio Barragán on Monday, making him the first Segunda División manager to be sacked this season, according to reports.The club had collected just two points from its opening four league matches and had not appointed a replacement at the time of reporting.Messi's potential arrival would therefore come while Eldense attempts to stabilise both its sporting and institutional situation.The proposed takeover also marks another intriguing development in Messi's post-playing career.The Argentine, who is now 39, has already won virtually every major honour available to him, including the World Cup and Champions League, and has collected a record eight Ballon d'Or awards.His investment in Cornellà earlier this year signalled his growing interest in football away from the pitch. A takeover of Eldense would represent a substantially larger commitment, putting one of the game's greatest-ever players in position to influence a club competing in Spain's professional second tier.For now, though, the key distinction is that Messi has reportedly reached an agreement in principle, rather than completed the acquisition.The final legal and contractual procedures, including due diligence and the required CSD authorisation, still need to be completed before Messi can officially take control of Eldense.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pellegrini: "Llegar a la Champions no es el fin, podemos demostrar que somos capaces de pasar de ronda"
articles.standfirst: El Ingeniero muestra su lado más ambicioso después de que el Betis se imponga al Lille
articles.summary: El Ingeniero muestra su lado más ambicioso después de que el Betis se imponga al Lille
articles.body: manuel Pellegrini, técnico del Betis, se mostró muy satisfecho con el rendimiento mostrado por su equipo en la visita al Lille con la que los verdiblancos arrancaban su aventura en la Champions League. Dos goles de Bartra y uno de Parrott le dieron a su equipo los primeros tres puntos de esta fase de liga en la que el Ingeniero no se conforma con estar. Quiere que su equipo compita y pelee hasta el final por pasar de ronda. El sueño de la Champions: "Más que un sueño era la capacidad de un grupo a través de unos méritos de clasificarse para una Champions que parecía inalcanzable. Lo conseguimos y el grupo no se conformó con eso. Hicimos un partido muy completo, tanto el primero tiempo, que no reflejó las ocasiones que hubo, y el segundo tiempo que estaban con uno menos pero salimos con la personalidad que hablamos independientemente de la competición que se dispute". Muchos años sin jugar la competición: "El Betis no había jugado hace muchos años la Champions League, hay jugadores que ya lo hicieron, yo también en mi carrera, y lo primero que hablamos es que llegar a la Champions no era la meta sino la personalidad que inculcamos de ir por la vitoria independiente de con quién juguemos. Partido muy completo, darle dos vueltas al marcador y la personalidad. Llevamos cinco años jugando en Europa y eso da experiencia también". Dominio del juego: "El control del partido jugando de visita lo tuvimos bastante amplio. En el 2-1 al descanso, tuvimos diez o doce disparos y ellos solo tres. El balón detenido iguala a toda la parte colectiva. Si revisas las estadísticas de posesión, llegadas y remates, el equipo superó al Lille y con personalidad en la forma de jugar". Goleadores: "Me alegro por ambos. Troy viene llegando a un club nuevo y marcar es importante. Y Marc, no es fácil cabecear así. Es un jugador de experiencia y eso sirve muchísimo a los jugadores que están comenzando. Él sabe exactamente lo que tiene que hacer en el campo". Objetivos del equipo: "Estamos en tres competiciones. Comenzamos en LaLiga con una derrota que pareció fea, pero el grupo se rearmó y consiguió tres puntos ante el Real Madrid. Ahora entramos en otra competición en la que no nos conformamos con participar, pero teníamos que demostrarlo en el campo. El equipo tiene personalidad para competir. ¿El mejor regalo para mi cumpleaños? Ganar el siguiente partido". Charla con Bartra durante el partido: "La experiencia es importante hacerla sentir en el campo. Si vamos ganando por uno y tenemos un córner en el minuto noventa y tantos, no debe ser un córner corto sino largo, para mantener los últimos minutos el balón. La charla no tiene más importancia que mantener el resultado". Plantilla completa: "Más que nombres, me ilusiona que el plantel mantenga el compromiso con lo que estamos haciendo. Faltan todavía jugadores importantes que tienen que ponerse a punto, como Lo Celso, Ceballos o Abde. Son jugadores que nos van a aportar en el futuro, pero ahora mismo, como les digo a ellos mismos, los más importantes son los que están". Reacción: "Hay que valorar lo que se consiguió la temporada pasada. Es la segunda vez que el Betis juega una Champions y eso hay que valorarlo, hay béticos que no habían nacido. Llegar a la Champions no es el fin, tenemos el convencimiento de que podemos demostrar en cada partido que somos capaces de pasar de ronda. Empezamos con buen pie, faltan muchísimos partidos y el plantel es consciente de lo que tiene que jugar y siempre exijo esa personalidad de hacerlo igual en el campo que sea".

articles.title: Lo que Courtois aprendió del gol de falta de Rashford y aplicó en el chut de Çalhanoglu: "Ya no me muevo"
articles.standfirst: El portero del Madrid analizó sus paradas y la victoria de su equipo ante el Inter
articles.summary: El portero del Madrid analizó sus paradas y la victoria de su equipo ante el Inter
articles.body: Courtois habló en Movistar tras la victoria del Real Madrid ante el Inter: "Al final jugamos contra un gran rival, el Inter es uno de los mejores equipos de Europa, el partido pudo ser 4-4, hemos aprovechado los errores suyos y ellos no han podido meter gol hasta muy tarde, pudimos cerrar el partido antes". La parada a Çalhanoglu en la falta: "Por mala suerte me metió Rashford en el Clásico en mi palo, que chutó muy bien pero me moví un poco. Con Lamine en el Mundial que tuvo una falta me quedé en mi palo y hoy igual. Si la mete por encima de la barrera hay que aplaudir, pero ya no me muevo de mi palo". Los defensas sufrieron: "Creo que más los centrocampistas, nos faltó control cuando hemos visto que no había ocasión clara, a lo mejor era mejor volver atrás y tener el control. El partido estuvo demasiado loco y es una cosa a mejorar". Falta de gol: "Contra el Betis era un partido para haber ganado pero nos faltó el gol y hoy también un poco. Hemos aprovechado sus fallos pero en jugadas libres nos ha faltado el gol y contra el Betis igual".

articles.title: Isco: "Hay que ir partido a partido y soñar en grande: la primera piedra ya la hemos puesto"
articles.standfirst: El malagueño, que "poco a poco" se va "sintiendo mejor", capitaneó al Betis frente al Lille
articles.summary: El malagueño, que "poco a poco" se va "sintiendo mejor", capitaneó al Betis frente al Lille
articles.body: Pese a que viene de una larguísima lesión, que le tuvo parado casi un año, y que el pasado viernes fue titular ante el Real Madrid, Pellegrini no quiso dejar pasar la oportunidad de contar esta noche con la experiencia de Isco Alarcón en el regreso del Betis a la Champions League tras más de 20 años de ausencia. El capitán jugó una hora de partido y dejó su sello con la asistencia a Bartra en el 2-2. Tras el encuentro, analizó en Movistar Liga de Campeones y Betis TV la gran remontada de su equipo. Gran victoria en la vuelta a la Champions: "Partido muy especial. Encontramos lo que veníamos buscando que era la victoria. Nos hemos repuesto bien de vernos dos veces por debajo en el marcador. Contento por los tres puntos y por volver a disfrutar de la mejor competición europea de clubes, y orgulloso de hacerlo como capitán del Betis". Personalidad de su equipo: "Competir hasta el máximo, intentar llegar lo más lejos posible y soñar en grande. Tenemos buen equipo, la primera piedra ya la hemos puesto porque ganar fuera de casa siempre es complicado. Hay que ir partido a partido y soñar en grande, como he dicho". Capacidad de reacción:. "Lo hemos demostrado muchas veces. Ojalá no tengamos que demostrarlo tanto. Al final sufrimos mucho. En este equipo se puede confiar, lo deja siempre todo en el campo, no bajamos los brazos y esa es la mentalidad que tenemos que tener. Es la diferencia entre un buen equipo y uno que quiere conseguir grandes cosas y ojalá sea un año redondo parta todos". Cómo se encuentra: "Poco a poco. Todavía me queda un poquito para tener el ritmo de mis compañeros, pero eso se gana con minutos en el campo. Me voy sintiendo mejor, sin dolor, cada vez con menos miedo que es algo que he sentido en los primeros días de pretemporada, en los primeros partidos, y ya lo voy perdiendo; eso es lo mejor de todo. Contento de volver a disfrutar del Betis y de la Champions".

articles.title: Deion Sanders Highlights Colorado's Latest 2-Way Player After Travis Hunter's Success
articles.summary: Colorado head coach Deion Sanders highlighted the two-way impact of lineman Chauncey Gooden during the team's season-opening 14-13 win over Georgia Tech.
articles.body:
Colorado head coach Deion Sanders highlighted the two-way impact of lineman Chauncey Gooden during the team's season-opening 14-13 win over Georgia Tech.

Sanders announced that Gooden "was the only interior lineman in all of Division I football that played both ways" on Tuesday, per USA Today's Brent Schrotenboer .

Sanders has plenty of experience coaching two-way players, as Travis Hunter earned Heisman Trophy honors in 2024 after excelling at both cornerback and wide receiver for the Buffaloes.

Report Card Grades for CFB's Top QBs 🧑‍🏫

As for Gooden, he started at guard while also spending time at defensive tackle against Georgia Tech.

Gooden put together an impressive performance, as he didn't allow a pressure or sack during the game (h/t Scott Procter of DNVR Sports). Colorado's defensive front also thrived in the win, amassing three sacks and limiting the Yellow Jackets to an average of 1.7 yards per rush as a team.

Gooden detailed the process that led to him becoming a two-way player when speaking to reporters on Tuesday.

"Coach Prime just believed in me on the field, whatever I'm doing," Gooden said. "First off, it was on the offensive line. So, he made it clear that I need to handle what I need to handle on the offensive side to be able to play defense. Defense is always something I've had the heart for."

"Coach Prime said you dominate on offense and then you'll be able to play defense," he added. "That's all I want to do. Anything to help my team win at the end of the day."

Gooden only appeared in four games during his freshman season in 2025, but it seems as though his role will continue to expand as the Buffaloes attempt to build upon their 1-0 start this year.

articles.title: Huijsen: "El año pasado fue difícil, ahora me siento más en casa"
articles.standfirst: El central disfruta de un buen momento tras un primer curso complicado
articles.summary: El central disfruta de un buen momento tras un primer curso complicado
articles.body: Dean Huijsen volvió a ser uno de los destacados en la victoria del Madrid ante el Inter. El malagueño está siendo uno de los pilares del Madrid en el arranque de la nueva temporada tras un primer curso complivcado tanto en lo colectivo como a nivel personal. El partido "No creo que haya habido un problema de juego. Creamos muchas ocasiones y al final por no meterlas el partido se volvió un poco loco. Tenemos que tener más control". La mano de Mou "Todo el mundo quiere que su central gane duelos. Está muy encima de mí y eso es bueno para todos". Los pitos a Vini "Vini sabe lo que es el Madrid, la exigencia de aquí. Todos sabemos lo bueno que es, va a trabajar más, siempre lo hace y siempre esá con una sonrisa. Lo del cambio ha sido por la nueva regla, a veces se nos puede olvidar". Volver a la selección "Lo de la selección no está en mis manos, sí jugar mucho y bien en el Madrid. Toca seguir, cinco partidos no son nada en el futbol, la temporada es de 50 o 60. Estoy bien, físicamente me siento mejor. Pero cinco partidos no son nada, hay que seguir así". La razón de su cambio "No medito ni nada de eso (risas). Al final, la magnitud del club cuando llegas no sabes lo que es. Ahora, aunque siempre hay cosas nuevas, pero estoy más acostumbrado, me siento más en casa. Mi carrera ha sido muy movida. Ahoar estoy bien, a seguir trabajando". Las críticas "La magnitud del Madrid es enorme, siempre se habla de nosotros para bien o para mal. Todos sabemos la exigencia que hay aquí, creo que estamos más unidos como grupo, el año pasado fue dificil". La inocencia del equipo "Tenemos que competir un poco mejor. Ves a los rivales, les hacen una faltya y dan tres vueltas, protestan y al final te llevas tú la amarilla. Tenmemos que mejorar en eso, al final el fútbol son emociones, también para el árbitro"

articles.title: SEC's hypocrisy on full display in LSU fight, but it might give league the chance to prove it can handle its own business
articles.summary: For decades, the SEC has been toothless in regulating its own schools. LSU and the band of loudmouth sycophants leading the university could have delivered t...
articles.body:
Among the many fascinating paragraphs buried in the SEC's amended federal lawsuit against LSU , one broadside against the school's administration and coach Lane Kiffin stands out for its unintended hilarity.

Behold: "[The SEC] Expressed great concern that LSU President [Wade] Rousse and Athletic Director [Verge] Ausberry have no meaningful control over Coach Kiffin or the football program at LSU."

Uh, hello! Earth to the SEC! Why do you think Kiffin took the job in the first place? You think they're paying him $13 million a year to be "meaningfully" controlled?

And goodness gracious, has anything else happened — other than the entire 93-year history of the conference — that might suggest SEC football coaches have never felt "meaningfully" controlled by their administrations?

A group of college presidents that for decades has found no way to deal with coaches and agents other than to get walked all over in contract negotiations, player discipline decisions and other measures of "meaningful" control now want to draw the line at Kiffin trying to play fast and loose with a couple NFL training camp cuts.

The SEC, of course, is right: If LSU isn't going to play by the rules the conference has agreed upon, then it shouldn't be in the conference. But finding religion now when you're the league that went to bat for Cam Newton 's reinstatement in 2010 because Auburn was going to win a national championship? When you're the league that sent commissioner Greg Sankey to Tennessee's committee on infractions hearing in 2023 as a warning not to punish them too hard for 18 Level 1 violations? When you've allowed the Bruce Pearls, Hugh Freezes and Bobby Petrinos back into your league after they made fools out of their former employers?

Hmm, what could possibly have given Kiffin the idea that SEC coaches are not meant to be "meaningfully" controlled as long as they win? Do you think Urban Meyer was "meaningfully" controlled at Florida? How about Nick Saban at Alabama?

There are not enough eye-rolls in the world to square the SEC's righteous anger at LSU and the actions of every other member school at one point or another. Expulsion threats? For trying to recruit a couple backups who got cut from NFL camps as rookies? Given the entire history of outlaw programs and scofflaw coaches?

It strains credulity to believe this sudden bout of piety, outside of the necessary threat level to get LSU to back down. And for goodness sakes, we all know if Kiffin had stayed at Ole Miss and tried to pull this same stunt, the same university president that is now aligned with colleagues in standing for the sanctity of the rulebook would be singing a much different tune. Keep in mind, Ole Miss was not offering Kiffin the moon and stars to stay up until the minute he signed his LSU contract last December because it had designs on "meaningfully" controlling who he wanted to recruit.

Having said that, as a simple matter of process and governance, this is an interesting and worthy experiment.

As we know, the SEC has been making noise about self-governance if Congress can't pass some kind of legislation with antitrust protection that would stop the flood of lawsuits every time the NCAA tries to enforce a rule.

I have been skeptical about the self-governance concept because the SEC — and particularly the SEC under commissioner Greg Sankey's leadership — has not very often acted like an organization that wants to play by any rules. Could the SEC really transform itself into an organization where it would have to sanction its own members, perhaps even severely?

History would tell you no. If anything, Sankey has been weakened internally over the last couple years by his inability to stop certain members from running to judges and attorney generals in an attempt to circumvent rules and spending caps that were negotiated by the schools themselves as part of the House v. NCAA settlement.

Among the many administrators in college athletics who have failed to exert "meaningful" control when it comes to the rulebook, the current SEC commissioner should go at the very top of that list.

But LSU and the band of loudmouth sycophants currently leading that university — including Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry — have delivered Sankey a chance to grab that control through their obstinance and arrogance.

After all, what would give the SEC the practical authority to start enforcing real rules? Suing one of their own members and winning in federal court would probably do the trick.

Just look at the statement the SEC released Tuesday alongside the legal complaint: "The SEC and its member universities have the right to establish, through agreed-upon governance procedures, the rules under which they voluntarily compete and to expect those rules to be followed."

The principle that these schools are part of a voluntary organization that plays by agreed-upon rules has always been true. They just didn't take it very seriously and tried to paint the NCAA as the bad guy when things went wrong, never acknowledging that the schools themselves are the NCAA.

Now they're saying that a self-governing organization works better when it has the right to administer meaningful punishments to people to break the rules — including, perhaps, expelling a longstanding member from the league? What a shocker.

If we could give truth serum to every president and athletic director in the SEC, it would be hard for any of them to make the case that the blowup over bringing back class of 2022 athletes who left for the NFL or NBA is actually about preserving fairness or preserving the ever-diminishing gap between college and pro.

Several schools in the SEC have $40 and $50 million football rosters. They are already pros.

But this is less about an ideological line than it is mapping out an endgame for the SEC. If the presidents are tired of being dragged into court every time they put a rule on the books that brings back some kind of order to their ecosystem, then they have two options.

The most straightforward way is to collectively bargain, which the university presidents are not ready to concede yet. So instead they'll try the second option first: Show that they can govern themselves as a conference.

The NCAA has lost its ability to govern not only because of aggressive lawyers and judges but because so many exceptions to rules have built up over time into a stew of contradictory precedents. It's much easier to argue that your client should get an extra year of this or a reduced penalty for that when you can take your pick of rules that the NCAA itself didn't bother to enforce.

The SEC, and the major conferences generally, are not burdened by that same track record. If you want to self-govern and have real authority to enforce rules, you have to be willing to go all the way to defend them or else it's like taking blocks out of a Jenga set until eventually it falls apart.

That's what the SEC is trying to convey here: Not only are we willing to enforce rules to the point of kicking LSU out of the conference, but we'll also get an injunction in federal court that blunts all the local judges and temporary restraining orders at the point of attack.

But despite the SEC's nauseating hypocrisy, you can't blame them for trying.

articles.title: Liverpool vs Atletico Madrid: Champions League – preview, teams, prediction
articles.summary: Andoni Iraola looks to build on his first win as Liverpool manager in tough game against Diego Simeone’s Atletico.
articles.body:
Who: Liverpool vs Atletico Madrid What: Champions League, league phase Where: Anfield, Liverpool, United Kingdom When: Wednesday, September 9, at 8pm (19:00 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 16:00 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream

Liverpool and Atletico Madrid kick off their 2026-27 Champions League campaigns with a mouthwatering league-phase game at Anfield.

Andoni Iraola got his first win as Liverpool manager over the weekend and now turns his attention to his first Champions League game with the football club.

Meanwhile, Atletico Madrid’s unbeaten start came to an end on Saturday when they slumped to a 3-0 away defeat at Athletic Bilbao.

Isak fires Liverpool to first win under Iraola

Alexander Isak struck twice in the opening 10 minutes as Liverpool delivered a first win for Iraola with a 2-0 victory at Ipswich on Friday.

Isak’s Premier League record 125-million-pound ($169m) move from Newcastle was matched this week by Manchester City’s signing of Enzo Fernandez, but 12 months on, the Swede is finally beginning to deliver on his price tag.

Ipswich never recovered from a disastrous start as Liverpool cruised to victory at Portman Road with their latest 100-million-pound ($135m) signing Bradley Barcola making his debut as a second-half substitute.

Victory maintains an unbeaten start for Iraola. A pair of 2-2 draws against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest did not lack in entertainment for the Basque coach’s opening two games in charge, but did little to ease doubts over Liverpool’s ability to challenge at the top end of the table this season.

“We needed it. Definitely needed this one. Also the way it has been, I think, with a clean sheet,” said Iraola.

Athletic Bilbao thumped Atletico Madrid 3-0 in La Liga on a miserable Saturday afternoon for Diego Simeone’s side.

Simeone’s Atletico fell to their first defeat of the season, putting up little fight in the second half after Athletic made the breakthrough with two quick strikes from Nico Williams and Robert Navarro, before Oihan Sancet added a third at Bilbao’s San Mames Stadium.

“[We had] two minutes of inattention and poor decision-making in situations we should have handled better,” said Simeone. “Bilbao capitalised on that lapse.”

Striker Julian Alvarez, who tried to leave the club to join Barcelona this summer, returned as a substitute after illness in an ineffective second-half appearance.

“We were good in the first half, but the game got away from us in those [couple of] minutes,” said Simeone.

“We lacked in the second half everything that we had in the first.”

The Opta supercomputer pegs Liverpool as the favourites, with a win probability of 53 percent. Atletico were given a 23.5 percent chance of winning.

The two clubs have faced each other on nine occasions; Liverpool won four of the games, Atletico won three, and two ended as draws.

September 17, 2025: Liverpool 3-2 Atletico Madrid (Champions League)

November 3, 2021: Liverpool 2-0 Atletico Madrid (Champions League)

October 19, 2021: Atletico Madrid 2-3 Liverpool (Champions League)

March 11, 2020: Liverpool 2-3 Atletico Madrid (Champions League)

February 18, 2020: Atletico Madrid 1-0 Liverpool (Champions League)

What happened the last time Liverpool played Atletico?

Liverpool seemed to be sailing with early goals from Andy Robertson and a typically fine strike by Mohamed Salah in their game last September, but were pegged back by Marcos Llorente’s goals in first-half stoppage time and at the 81st minute.

However, Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk soared to score with a header in the second minute of stoppage time to seal a 3-2 win for the Reds.

Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni have all been ruled out with injuries, while Federico Chiesa and Wataru Endo were not included in Liverpool’s Champions League squad.

Joe Gomez faces a late fitness test as he is struggling with a muscle issue.

New signing Bradley Barcola may be set for his start out wide on the right, with Victor Munoz dropping to the bench.

Forward Alexander Sorloth is expected to miss out on the game due to a thigh injury, and Arnau Ortiz is suspended after receiving a red card while last in European action – for Slask Wroclaw back in August 2024.

articles.title: Napoli vs Arsenal: Champions League – prediction, teams, lineups
articles.summary: Napoli has issues in midfield for its Champions League opener against Arsenal, but hope to recover Serie A winning form.
articles.body:
Who: Napoli vs Arsenal What: UEFA Champions League Where: Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples, Italy When: Wednesday at 9pm local time (1900GMT). How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 16:00 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream.

Napoli and Arsenal are paired in titanic tussle to open their Champions League seasons as two league winners – in Serie A and the Premier League respectively – within the last two-season faceoffs.

The Gunners ended a 22-year wait to reclaim the English top flight last season, while also reaching the Champions League final where they were defeated by Paris Saint-Germain.

Napoli were dethroned as Italian champions by Inter Milan last season, but retain a squad capable of striking fear into any side in Europe.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at the mouth-watering matchup.

As the defending Serie A champion last season, Napoli was eliminated in the league phase after finishing 30th of the 36 teams in the Champions League.

Massimiliano Allegri replaced Antonio Conte as head coach after last season.

“We need to get 12 points to secure qualification,” Allegri said. “We know we’re up against a team that has just won the Premier League and reached the final of this competition. [Arsenal manager Mikel] Arteta has done well to get his defence organized and they concede very few goals.

“I had the fortune of [coaching] in two finals but I lost both of them,” Allegri said, referring to when he was at Juventus and the 2015 and 2017 finals, which were won by Barcelona and Real Madrid, respectively.

Napoli has lost two straight in Serie A, getting beat by Como and Inter Milan – going down 3-2 to the latter at the weekend.

How have Premier League champions Arsenal started the new season?

Arsenal are on a four-game winning streak to start their latest campaign.

The Gunners beat Manchester City 3-0 in the Community Shield – the English season opener between the previous season’s league and cup winners – to start the run.

Coventry, Aston Villa and Chelsea have been downed in the league, in what has been a formidable start.

Nine goals have been scored so far, with only one conceded by the team not only regarded as the best defence in the world, but also the favourites lift the Champions League trophy.

The Opta supercomputer has given Arsenal a 52 percent chance of winning the game, while offering Napoli only a 22 percent chance.

This will be the fifth meeting between the teams with Arsenal winning three of the encounters and Napoli claiming victory in the other match.

October 1, 2013: Champions League – Arsenal 2–0 Napoli

December 11, 2013: Champions League – Napoli 2–0 Arsenal

April 11, 2019: Europa League – Arsenal 2–0 Napoli

April 18, 2019: Europa League – Napoli 0–1 Arsenal

Napoli has issues in midfield for its Champions League opener against Arsenal on Wednesday, with both Scott McTominay and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa unavailable.

McTominay underwent a surgical procedure to treat an irregular heartbeat on Tuesday, while Anguissa has a physical issue.

“In midfield we will play three between (Kevin) De Bruyne, (Billy) Gilmour, (Stanislav) Lobotka and (Antonio) Vergara,” Napoli coach Allegri said Tuesday.

Meret; Di Lorenzo, Marin, Rrahmani, Spinazzola; De Bruyne, Lobotka, Gilmour; Politano, Hojlund, Santos

Cristhian Mosquera has not travelled for the match due to a muscular injury that kept him out of the Aston Villa game.

Jurrien Timber continues his return from a groin injury and could make the bench. William Saliba remains out with a back problem.

Bruno Guimaraes, who was an unused sub at the weekend, is closing on full fitness.

Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Zubimendi, Rice; Saka, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz

articles.title: Yes, the SEC really could 'terminate' LSU. Here's an inside look at the fight that could reshape college football
articles.summary: The SEC evicting LSU from the league would serve as an unprecedented move that will invariably cause ripple effects across the country.
articles.body:
Imagine for a second that the most anticipated SEC football game in many years is not actually an SEC football game at all.

If SEC presidents and chancellors vote to expel LSU from the conference on Thursday — there is a scheduled vote — and if that decision would take effect immediately, the LSU-Ole Miss football game in Oxford next Saturday would transform into a non-conference game, one person within the league suggested.

"The game may not be played at all," another stakeholder quipped.

The ramifications don't stop there, of course. The SEC evicting from the league a longstanding member would serve as an unprecedented move that will invariably cause ripple effects across the country. The school stands to lose millions in conference distribution, have its schedule of games stripped and path to championships blocked — all over their intentions to potentially add professional football and basketball players to their rosters.

Those in Baton Rouge are somewhat mystified.

The program did not add to its football roster those aforementioned professional players. So, what are the grounds for booting the school from the league?

Well, for one, the league does not need grounds or reasoning, according to the bylaws. But the conference, in a federal lawsuit against the school filed in Alabama, did spell out some reasons: LSU left open roster spots to possibly, at a later date, add those aforementioned players; coach Lane Kiffin suggested through comments in various media availabilities that he recruited pro players while knowing it is against the rules; and the university leadership, despite voting for the SEC's pro-player ban, has mostly remained on the sideline as its coach pursues such rule-breaking.

The SEC's legal filing asks a judge to permit the conference to enforce its rules by, potentially, expelling the school from the league. And while that's stunning to see in print, none of us should be too surprised, unless of course you missed a story at Yahoo Sports last week revealing this as a possibility that conference leaders have been discussing now for more than a week.

A hearing is set for 1 p.m. CT Wednesday in Birmingham, where a judge may open a path for the SEC to enforce such sanctions upon the Tigers.

What's lingering over all of this is what LSU can do to prevent such a vote from happening on Thursday. Common sense tells us this can be rectified if school administrators indicate they will follow the rules.

Perhaps that means president Wade Rousse releases a public statement announcing that the school will abide by SEC guidance and not add pro players to the roster. Or maybe he sends the SEC's legal team a formal note that says such.

The pro players recruited by LSU are part of a class of athletes who won an injunction last week from a Louisiana judge granting them a fifth season of eligibility to return to college after signing pro contracts this summer. As part of that ruling, LSU is prohibited from taking any action that negatively impacts those players (such as, you know, not adding them to the roster after promising them a spot!).

Coach Will Wade's basketball team plans to add to its roster RJ Luis, who played in three NBA games and won an injunction in a separate Louisiana court ruling.

This is a Louisiana-versus-the-SEC moment that reaches toward the highest rung of state government.

Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry described the SEC's threats as "ridiculous," and asked, "Can we just play football?" Well, LSU did, in fact, play football last week, opening its season with an evisceration of Clemson, 51-10 , in Tiger Stadium.

The Tigers are good enough that one LSU staff member quipped on Tuesday, "I would get rid of us too if we played like that in our first game."

Other politicians are coming to the support of their state's biggest brand. Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.) called for the SEC to apply its rules consistently and described the SEC's approach to the LSU situation as a "hypocrisy" that is unfair to college athletes.

"The SEC is threatening LSU while the same conference allows athletes who spent YEARS competing professionally in foreign leagues to play immediately," Cassidy wrote, perhaps a nod to the Charles Bediako situation at Alabama in the spring.

But will the SEC really do it? Will the SEC kick out of the league, in the middle of football season, one of its biggest brands in the sport? Will the league boot a football program that's won three national championships since 2003, a baseball team that claimed titles in two of the last four seasons, and women's basketball and gymnastics teams that won it all in 2023 and 2024, respectively?

In all, the university has claimed 53 team national titles.

Surely, the conference would not hit the eject button on this, right?

"This," said one administrator within the conference Tuesday, "is real."

In fact, the SEC presidents met on Aug. 30 without LSU on the call — the first real sign that something big was brewing. They discussed the plethora of options as reported in that Aug. 31 story from Yahoo Sports: a boycott of LSU, a suspension or probation, and, yes, expulsion. The group met again on Friday, a day before LSU's season opener, to continue those discussions, digging deeper into the legal maneuvers necessary to make such an unprecedented move happen.

The presidents need 11 supportive votes from the 16 schools to expel a member. For more than a week now — since that Aug. 30 gathering — the belief is that they have the necessary votes to place LSU on probation at the very least, if not fully booting the university.

In fact, at least a couple executives at SEC schools have suggested to their ACC brethren that there might be a spot open in the league soon.

"There are plenty of other schools who will take their place," said one high-ranking SEC university leader to Yahoo Sports.

If you've been following realignment discussions, you know that several ACC programs are itching to leave the conference and join the SEC. Two of them, in fact, filed a lawsuit against the league: Florida State and Clemson.

Another, North Carolina, is probably the most attractive replacement, according to many in the SEC. And others, like Miami, Georgia Tech and Virginia, are interesting options that have kept their intentions more private.

This whole situation unfolds at an intriguing time in the sport's landscape.

The SEC's aggressive approach to LSU is seen as the first test of a potential conference-wide governance framework, a long-discussed concept in the league where it creates and enforces its own rules separate from the NCAA to limit legal challenges. Permitting a member school to already, even before the league-wide governance model is established, break conference policies would jeopardize the viability of any new governance concept.

So, yes, says one SEC president, this is serious.

"It is time," the president said, "for everyone to follow SEC rules."

articles.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold: Real Madrid right-back returns to midfield
articles.summary: Trent Alexander-Arnold started in midfield for Real Madrid's win over Inter - but Jose Mourinho says it is not his best position.
articles.body:
It's the question that just doesn't seem to go away - can Trent Alexander-Arnold really work in midfield?

Gareth Southgate played him there for England during Euro 2024 before ending the experiment after only two group games.

Jurgen Klopp's entire Liverpool gameplan relied on his ability to step into the middle and spray passes around... albeit from a starting position of right-back.

And now Jose Mourinho has become the latest manager to dabble, picking the 27-year-old in midfield for Real Madrid's Champions League win over Inter Milan on Tuesday.

Having struggled to establish himself as Real's first-choice full-back since moving to the Bernabeu last summer, could this be the moment he finally clicks in the middle of the park?

"He has played midfield with England and Liverpool... but he is not a midfielder," insisted Mourinho after his side's edgy 2-1 win.

"He has played very well. He has interpreted what he needed to really well, tactically.

"Both him and Valverde have worked very well at this level."

So while Mourinho was "very grateful" for Alexander-Arnold's efforts in the middle, don't expect to see him play there on a regular basis.

Mbappe goes joint-fifth in all-time list as Real Madrid beat Inter

The former Liverpool player's inclusion in midfield was largely circumstantial, with suspensions for Eduardo Camavinga, Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva leaving Mourinho short on options.

Alexander-Arnold lined up alongside Federico Valverde but had a mixed evening, creating two chances and attempting more crosses than any other Real player - but failing to win a tackle. His passing accuracy was also down at 83.3%.

He was substituted shortly after Inter pulled one back on 77 minutes, prompting whistles around the stadium - although this could well have been frustration Madrid supporters felt at their team's performance rather than at Alexander-Arnold individually.

It was the first competitive match in which Alexander-Arnold and fellow right-back Denzel Dumfries had started together. He started both for a pre-season friendly against Fiorentina, with Alexander-Arnold operating at right-back while Dumfries played further forward on the same side.

It is clear Mourinho still doesn't have a definite starting right-back, so in the same way Alexander-Arnold had to fight to start with Dani Carvajal last season, he is doing the same this season with Dumfries.

But BBC Sport understands the Portuguese has been impressed by the England international's performances, values and the versatility he brings to the squad.

Indeed, Mourinho views Alexander-Arnold as different from many traditional full-backs because of his ability to move into central areas and contribute to attacks from midfield positions.

His passing, crossing, through balls and set-piece delivery remain among the strongest parts of his game.

'He left the pitch with nothing left to give'

While Southgate's attempts to convert him into a central player at Euro 2024 ultimately ended in him being dropped from the team, Alexander-Arnold has had some success there in the past.

In June 2023, he was handed the England number 10 shirt for a qualifier in Malta, a game which the Three Lions won 4-0 - and in which Alexander-Arnold himself scored from midfield.

"It feels natural, I will say that. It's somewhere I can see myself playing."

Southgate continued to flirt with playing him in that position during the course of the next 12 months, before abandoning the plan after an underwhelming 1-1 draw with Denmark. Alexander-Arnold was brought off before the hour-mark.

After Tuesday's win over Inter, Mourinho admitted the position still caused some difficulties.

"He has lost some balls because it is not the same to play in this position compared to at right-back," he said.

"The intensity of physical work is quite difficult. He has a different engine. He has given 100%. He left the pitch with nothing left to give."

articles.title: Dabo Swinney rebukes reporter who asked about Clemson's roster construction days after lopsided Week 1 loss to LSU
articles.summary: Swinney accused the reporter of stirring the pot in the wake of the Tigers' 51-10 season-opening defeat.
articles.body:
This summer, Clemson found itself outside the preseason AP Top 25 for the first time since 2011. Even so, the Tigers were just a handful of votes shy of the No. 25 ranking.

Now, three days after its 51-10 defeat to a newly eighth-ranked LSU , Clemson isn't even in the receiving votes section of the AP poll . Embarrassed in the SEC's Death Valley, the Tigers retreated back to their abode, which, at the moment, is hardly the intimidating environment it's been for most of Dabo Swinney's 19-season head-coaching tenure.

Swinney is 7-8 in his last 15 games at the helm, dating back to a first-round College Football Playoff loss to Texas at the end of the 2024 campaign. The shine of his two national titles is growing dim in the NIL and transfer portal era, and his relentless positivity is falling on deaf ears not even two weeks into September.

Swinney is under fire, and his latest news conference tirade is fanning the flames warming his seat.

The State's Chapel Fowler asked Swinney on Tuesday if he regretted anything about his offseason roster construction right now.

Swinney, who began chuckling and sporting a wry smile as the question neared its end, responded: "Chapel, you come with all these questions. I'll tell ya. You're 'the gotcha guy.'"

Swinney continued, turning to the question at hand: "No, I don't. I don't, man. I regret being 0-1 right now. I regret that. But, no, we're uh — can you ask me that at the end of the season? You know? The season ain't over. I mean, we [played] one game. We've got 11 more.

"What if we go 11-1? You promise me you'll ask me that then?"

"OK good," Swinney said. "I'll answer it, alright. But I'm not answering questions like that, Chapel. I know that's your role in this environment to be the guy that wants to create all the controversy and ask the controversial questions. If that's who you are, that's fine. I get it."

Swinney went on: "But I'll answer that at the end of the season — we played one game. One game. Alright?"

Swinney then proceeded to ask Fowler if he played football.

"They give you 12 games," Swinney said. "And at the end of the year, you count 'em up. That's when those type of questions are fair, to me, not after one game, to maybe the best team in the country. … Other people have good teams and coaches and things like that, too. So give them credit."

Swinney, trying to shift the focus to a Week 2 home matchup versus Georgia Southern, concluded: "We've got 11 more games to go battle, and then we'll count 'em up. And then you can ask me whatever question you want."

While Swinney waded deeper into the transfer portal waters than in years past — adding a program-record 13 portal and JUCO players this offseason — he notably didn't bring in a transfer quarterback. Plus, the Tigers didn't reel in a single offensive lineman in the portal despite losing four starters up front from the 2025 squad.

Clemson was outgained 644-145 on Saturday in Baton Rouge. Clemson conceded four sacks, and its two quarterbacks — senior Christopher Vizzina and freshman Tait Reynolds — both struggled, with neither averaging more than 5.2 yards per pass attempt.

articles.title: Takeaways for Penn State football following Week 1 shutout of Marshall

articles.body:
HAPPY VALLEY, Pa. (WHTM) -- Clear and consistent communication was a marker for success for Penn State football in its season-opening 45-0 win over Marshall .

For so many players and coaches, it was their first experience playing inside West Shore Home Field at Beaver Stadium, so playing with limited mistakes gave them a ton of confidence headed into week two on the road against Temple .

"The ability to make in-game adjustments as a coaching staff with new players and then the ability for our players to communicate on the field, and I thought we did some really good things that way. Then I think, on the second thing of it, playing in complementary football, think those things are what great football teams have the ability to do," head coach Matt Campbell said.

That complementary football, thanks in part to a lockdown defense that allowed just 44 rushing yards, which defensive coordinator D'Anton Lynn said contributed to the tone set by the interior defensive line.

"There's still a lot more left on the plate, there's a couple things we left, technical, technique-wise, as a group, but our whole defense did a good job," senior defensive tackle Siale Taupaki said.

Lynn opted to call the plays from the press box instead of down on the field.

"I spent the majority of my time in the NFL in the booth, and I just felt like, with the coaches we had on the field, I trust all those guys and just, in-between drives, just felt like, man, you are able to gather so much more information," Lynn said.

Perhaps the biggest lesson to learn in week 2 is how to travel. The Nittany Lions get the opportunity to play on the road in Chicago, Ann Arbor and Seattle later in the season during Big Ten play.

articles.title: MAC commish Jon Steinbrecher: Replay officials instructed to use game feed of clock, not replay feed
articles.summary: MAC commissioner says correct protocol was not followed.
articles.body:
Mid-American Conference commissioner Jon Steinbrecher watched the final seconds of the Sept. 12 matchup between Western Michigan and Michigan at Michigan Stadium on television. Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood 's Hail Mary on the previous play sailed out of the end zone, and there was no time left on the clock viewers saw on the NBC television feed.

"I was certain that the play would be reviewed," Steinbrecher told The Sporting News. "From there, you're off to the races. You don't know what it's going to show."

Did anybody expect what happened next? Following an official review that put one second back on the clock, the Wolverines beat the Broncos 13-12 on Sept. 12 on a 47-yard Hail Mary pass from Underwood to JJ Buchanan . On Tuesday, the MAC submitted formal appeals to the FBS oversight committee and the College Football Playoff requesting that Western Michigan be recognized as the winner of the game.

"You're disappointed it's not being recorded as a 'W' right now," Steinbrecher said. "I think (Western Michigan) made a statement that people will remember."

Steinbrecher explained what was behind that decision to appeal in an interview with The Sporting News.

MAC commissioner discusses appeal of Western Michigan-Michigan

The MAC reversed its previous stance with a new statement that read:. "It is now evident that replay protocol was not followed in determining whether time remained on the game clock" at the end of the Michigan-Western Michigan game.

The statement says the Big Ten replay crew used the clock feed in its replay system – not the game clock displayed on NBC.

Is two separate clock feeds the major issue at hand for Steinbrecher?

"Correct," Steinbrecher said. "There is a protocol to be followed. We're instructed to utilize the game feed. Now, it's a unique situation here. I think the Big Ten may be the only one who is using a replay system that has a feed coming in that includes a clock in it so it has a clock within their replay system. That's kind of where we're at."

The MAC initially accepted the Big Ten's explanation for putting one second back on the clock after the game. Steinbrecher said the social media backlash did not make an impact on the MAC's decision to appeal.

"It was working the process," Steinbrecher said. "You take the information you have in the moment, and you make the best choices you can off that information. Then, you continue to seek and gather information to verify or refute where you're at. You continue to do that. Let's make sure this is buttoned up."

Steinbrecher continues to do work with Western Michigan school officials. On Tuesday, Western Michigan president Russ Kavalhuna released a statement that said : "We can respect the game while asking serious questions."

Steinbrecher said he admires how Western Michigan has handled the situation – including the players and coach Lance Taylor. The MAC commissioner also continues to have conversations with the Big Ten.

"I've had great conversations with the Big Ten and all that," Steinbrecher said." Everyone has been open on these things. I think there might just be a difference of opinion."

The Big Ten also released a statement Tuesday:

"The Big Ten stands by the statement released following the conclusion of the Western Michigan at Michigan game and the determination made by the replay officials. We will have no further comment on the matter."

Impact of MAC's appeal of Western Michigan-Michigan game

Steinbrecher – who took over as MAC commissioner in 2009 – has been on the winning side of a controversial Hail Mary finish against a Power 4 school. On Sept. 10, 2016, Central Michigan beat Oklahoma State 30-27 after a rule interpretation led to an extra down.

"I can almost guarantee that everybody — that most conferences — we've all had experiences when they've favored you and not favored you," Steinbrecher said.

On Tuesday, Michigan dropped out of the AP Top 25. The Wolverines received 69 votes. The Broncos received 12 votes. Steinbrecher said some new protocol questions must be answered in the aftermath of the Michigan-Western Michigan result regardless of the result of the appeal.

"That's part and parcel of all of this," Steinbrecher said. "Any time you have situations like that, we ought to be informed by them and let's learn from them and what processes, policies and procedures we can put in place to assist us if it would arise again."

That could entail a few tweaks — like adding tenths of a second to the game clock – but the issue at hands remains. There has to be one clock – not two – in the future.

"Would it be appropriate to put in tenths of seconds?" Steinbrecher asked. "We went through all that in the basketball world, right? We ultimately got there. I have no doubt we'll end up discussing that whether we'll get there or not. We clearly have to come to an agreement that all of us will use — if there are multiple feeds of clocks — what clock is being the ultimate arbiter? We've got to have agreement on that."

Only time will tell you whether Robinson or Jahmyr Gibbs (or neither) was the right call at 1.01 this season, but there's little reason to think that Atlanta 's star can't shine in the season opener.

Gibbs was the only RB to score 20 PPR points against the Steelers last season, so maybe there's a slight matchup downgrade, but I'm not even sold on that (fifth most yards per carry allowed to running backs after contact inside the red zone last season).

We aren't 100% sure what to expect from this offense, but we know it'll all revolve around #7, and until we see the NFL consistently figure out a way to slow his efficiency, I'll be penciling him in for 100+ scrimmage yards with a better chance to find paydirt than to be held out of the paint (34 TDs in 51 career games).

This week should be fine by his lofty standards: Panthers, Packers , and Saints over the next three games could be downright dominant for the player I had atop my preseason rankings.

There's a lot to like here, but you didn't draft Corum with the thought that he'd be an asset from the jump. He averaged 5.1 YPC a season ago, and the best offense in the sport didn't hesitate to take Kyren Williams off the field for drives at a time to get him work.

Heck, he led the Rams in rushing in the NFC Title game against the Seahawks.

At cost, I thought he was the proper play in this backfield over the summer, and while I'm not budging off of that take, I'm not playing him until we have some 2026 data points.

The skill set limitations are a bit of a concern, especially if regression hits this offense as a whole. For his career, just 15 of his 216 touches have come through the air, and his next 15-yard reception at the professional level will be his first.

Your investment here was one with the long game in mind. Sit tight and be patient. I'm not sure he'll hit double digits in the touch department this week, and even if that is the case, nothing should change in how you view Corum: you're projecting growth as the season progresses and hoping that you can churn a profit when it matters most.

Here's a fun split for you to bring up at the Week 1 watch party when your friends ask you why you want to have the Jets/Titans on a TV.

Games decided by 3 or fewer points: 18.0 PPG

I like this game for one reason and one reason only: it's a chance to see the stars shine. It's going to be rare that either of these teams are in competitive games that allow for that to happen in an honest way, so yea, I'm excited to see what happens in this spot.

I haven't yet decided how to best do it (it hinges more on the lineup construction that I land on and you can see that in our FREE fantasy/betting newsletter that releases four times a week), but I'm going to have a skinny stack in this game with a player from both sides.

Hall is talented enough to be in consideration for that, though I currently project the Titans to win and thus am leaning in favor of their running game. Tennessee 's defense isn't bad, and in terms of yards allowed per carry before contact to running backs, they were actually the best in the sport (35.2% better than league average).

Hall can beat any defense with enough bites at the apple, and I expect that to be the case this weekend. I have him ranked as a RB1 for Sunday and already have him penciled in as a sell-high candidate.

It'll be easy. You sell your opposition on his raw talent and maybe even average offensive support. You get the highlight tape from this weekend and run it on a loop.

This is a player that has the potential to be a top-10 running back for the season from a talent perspective; that's not in question.

It's also not the question we are asking.

There are no points awarded for talent and if/when this offense becomes predictable due to game script (three straight games against the offensively charged NFC North certainly could cause that once we put a bow on Week 1), we are at risk of it being a coin flip if he's a viable RB2 (eight games last season as a top-24 option and eight outside of that).

Start him this week and sell him for a WR2 that you could see sustaining WR1 production next week.
